title: Repair the ledger's seal: refuse a glob/pattern entry in a task's allowed_paths at contract time, claim and submit so every new packet binds literal tracked paths and the content identity covers what the packet declares; add the CI static catch and a frozen grandfather allowlist for the pre-existing pattern-carrying tasks; produce a look-back report of accepted tasks whose identities bound less than their packets said; this task does NOT expand patterns at identity time, does NOT rewrite any old task/gate/directive record, and does NOT change any workflow or touch .claude/** [backlog DB-181; owner D-090-R557; D-001-R146, D-001-R110]
objective: Close backlog row DB-181: the registry builds a task's content identity from LITERAL git paths, so an allowed_paths entry written as a glob/pattern binds no file, and a task whose paths are all patterns is bound only by its literal report once the report placeholder is tracked. FACTS TODAY, with file and line. (1) tools/directive_registry.py:_run_git (line ~1307) runs git with GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, so every pathspec is matched literally; _ls_tree_entries (line ~1373) and git_tree_manifest (line ~1404) therefore resolve a pattern to zero tracked objects. (2) frozen_git_identity (line ~1605) hashes those entries plus the control-plane material entries; its empty-identity guard (line ~1673) refuses ONLY when BOTH components are empty, so a task that carries a literal report under project-control/reports/ passes even when every real-code entry is a pattern. (3) tools/project_control.py:_task_git_identity (line ~375) is the single identity function submit (line ~523), gate and accept (_directive_accept_reasons, line ~552/563) all call; accept recompares the live identity to the frozen report's content_manifest_sha256. (4) tools/validate_directive_compliance.py:_validate_empty_identity (c17, line ~273) recomputes git_tree_manifest at HEAD but only checks EMPTINESS; the validator never recomputes-and-compares an accepted task's full identity (c10 compares stored sha to stored sha). (5) scripts/lanes/check_lane_paths.py does NOT read task allowed_paths (it checks diff paths against lane patterns), and no hook under .claude/hooks/ reads allowed_paths. VERIFIED NUMBERS (reproduce them read-only against the checkout before editing and record them): 'docs/measurement-basis/**' resolves to 0 tracked files, 'docs/measurement-basis' resolves to 7; 'docs/measurement-basis/*' and 'result_way_bridge_*.py' resolve to 0. CHOSEN REPAIR = OPTION B (refuse a pattern, do NOT expand it at identity time). STEP 1 - add one shared detector in tools/directive_registry.py, pattern_allowed_paths(allowed_paths) -> list of offending entries, placed beside path_free_opt_in so the CLI and the validator can never diverge (D-001-R152 precedent). An entry is a non-binding PATTERN when it contains '*' or '?' or begins with ':' (pathspec magic). An entry is NOT a pattern merely because it contains '[' or ']': the repository tracks one legitimate literal bracket path (apps/web/src/app/survey/review/[documentId]/page.tsx, a Next.js dynamic route that binds correctly under literal pathspecs); state the bracket-only char-range residual as a documented limitation rather than false-flagging that route. STEP 2 - add one frozen grandfather allowlist constant in tools/directive_registry.py, built by running your own look-back script at the claim-seam head over project-control/tasks/*.json: the exact set of task ids that already carry at least one pattern entry (accepted AND in-flight). These packets are NOT rewritten (forbidden); the allowlist exempts exactly them so the refusal bites only NEW packets and so validate_directive_compliance.py --check stays exit 0. STEP 3 - wire the refusal: tools/project_control.py claim (beside _directive_claim_check, line ~854) and submit (before/at _task_git_identity, line ~523) fail closed naming the offending entry and the fix ('name the folder or the existing file literally') UNLESS the task id is in the frozen allowlist; tools/validate_directive_compliance.py adds a new static check (model it on c17) that flags a pattern entry in any in-regime, non-grandfathered task packet. Do NOT modify the empty-identity guard, the identity algorithm, _ls_tree_entries, git_tree_manifest or GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS. ORCHESTRATOR READINGS (take as given, do not re-derive): D-090-R557 obliges the repair; D-001-R146/R110 define the identity this task protects; the empty-identity guard already catches the all-pattern-no-literal case, so the only gap is the insidious patterns-plus-literal-report case. TESTS (one per input state, with a table in the producer report): write the RED proof FIRST - a task whose allowed_paths are all patterns is accepted at contract/claim today and REFUSED after the change (run it against the pre-change code and show it fails to refuse). Then one test per state: a literal existing file (accepted), a literal existing folder (accepted), a 'folder/**' entry (refused), a 'name_*.py' entry (refused), a literal path that does not exist yet (NOT refused as a pattern - emptiness is a separate guard), a mix of literal and pattern (refused, naming the pattern entry), an empty allowed_paths list (the detector is a no-op; the existing path-free/empty-identity guard is unchanged), and the bracket route apps/web/src/app/survey/review/[documentId]/page.tsx (NOT refused). MIGRATION PROOF: run python tools/validate_directive_compliance.py --check with a DIRECT exit code BEFORE and AFTER the change and show it exits 0 both times (it runs in ~49s here); state exactly what recomputation acceptance and the validator perform on old tasks (accept recomputes the full identity only at the moment a task is accepted, never re-run on an already-accepted task; the validator recomputes only emptiness and never compares an accepted task's full identity), and that Option B changes no identity value so no accepted task's recorded identity moves. MUTATION PROOF: with the refusal reverted to the literal pre-change code, the red proof and the three refusal-state tests fail. NO-WEAKENING: no existing test deleted, skipped, xfailed or loosened; no existing check weakened; the empty-identity guard, c17, and the identity algorithm are byte-unchanged. WINDOWS: state that path handling is posix-string comparison with no OS call and is Windows-safe, but do NOT claim it tested on Windows (no Windows run here). Run python tools/modularity_check.py --check and record its exit code; directive_registry.py is already 1790 lines - keep the addition small and cohesive and record a cohesion justification if the check flags it, do NOT split the file in this task. NOT IN THIS TASK: expanding patterns at identity time (Option A, rejected - it would reintroduce the glob/pathspec expansion that GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 deliberately removed as G5 hardening, would silently bind files a typo names, and would change the identity a pattern produces); rewriting, re-accepting, or re-validating any old task, gate, verification or directive record; rewriting the in-flight pattern-carrying packets; changing any workflow, CI lane check, or hook; touching .claude/** ; running tools/test_directive_compliance.py as a whole (hours) - run only the named focused tests.
business_reason: Owner directive D-090-R557 (message 113, 2026-10-07): the ledger-sealing defect in the content identity stays tracked until repaired and a repair task is contracted. Until it is repaired a packet can declare code scope with a pattern that binds nothing, so the hash that submission, the gates and acceptance compare can cover far less than the packet claims - the seal the whole control plane leans on. The repair also permanently enforces DB-181's interim rule (every packet names its folders and existing files literally) and serves D-001-R146 and D-001-R110, which require the reviewed identity to cover the task's declared content.
